finding.summary: Session serialization accumulates the complete, potentially large session payload in a default growable MemoryStream.
finding.explanation: CommitAsync serializes every key and value into a default MemoryStream with repeated writes and no validated capacity bound, then calls ToArray for an additional full copy. Large or bursty session state can therefore cause geometric backing-array growth, LOH pressure, and high peak memory on the request path.

finding.summary: Authentication properties serialize through an unbounded growable MemoryStream.
finding.explanation: Serialize writes all authentication property entries into a default MemoryStream without a validated capacity or serialized-size bound and then calls ToArray. Large property collections or values can cause repeated growth copies and a second exact-size allocation.

finding.summary: Render-tree keyed lookup probes each old sibling key before inserting it.
finding.explanation: BuildKeyToInfoLookup calls ContainsKey(key) to detect a duplicate and then assigns result[key] for the same key. The pooled plain Dictionary therefore hashes and probes every nonduplicate old key twice on a render-diff path. A single TryAdd-style operation can preserve duplicate detection and exception behavior while avoiding the second probe.

finding.summary: Password validation uses LINQ All to scan every UTF-16 character.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync routes the non-alphanumeric requirement through Enumerable.All over the password string. This is a reusable validation path and the predicate is a simple character test; a direct indexed loop preserves short-circuiting and works across every target framework without LINQ iterator and delegate overhead.

finding.summary: Password digit validation uses LINQ Any over the string.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync enumerates password characters through Enumerable.Any for a simple digit predicate. A direct indexed loop is portable to the project’s .NET Framework, netstandard2.0, and modern .NET targets and preserves the existing UTF-16 char semantics and short-circuiting.

finding.summary: Password lowercase validation uses LINQ Any over the string.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync enumerates password characters through Enumerable.Any for a simple lowercase predicate. A direct indexed loop avoids LINQ enumeration while preserving short-circuiting and exact char-category behavior on all target frameworks.

finding.summary: Password uppercase validation uses LINQ Any over the string.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync enumerates password characters through Enumerable.Any for a simple uppercase predicate. A direct indexed loop avoids LINQ enumeration while preserving short-circuiting and exact char-category behavior on all target frameworks.

finding.summary: Username validation enumerates the username with LINQ and searches the allowed-character string for every character.
finding.explanation: ValidateUserName runs for each Identity user validation operation. Its Any predicate enumerates the string through LINQ, and each predicate invocation performs another sequential character search over the configurable AllowedUserNameCharacters string. A direct indexed loop can preserve the current UTF-16 char semantics, null/empty handling, and short-circuit behavior without LINQ iterator/delegate overhead.

finding.summary: Stream IDs are accumulated in a temporary List and immediately copied to an array.
finding.explanation: ReadStreamIds knows streamIdCount before parsing, but allocates a growable List<string>, appends every ID, then allocates and copies again with ToArray. The list is only an intermediate adapter for the string[] return value on the per-message MessagePack parse path. Allocate the final array from streamIdCount and fill it directly while preserving null-for-empty behavior and validation order.

finding.summary: Authentication ticket serialization grows a MemoryStream and then copies the complete ticket.
finding.explanation: Serialize writes a ticket with variable identity, claim, property, and string counts through BinaryWriter into a default MemoryStream, then returns ToArray. The source does not enforce a local serialized-size bound, so unusually large tickets can cause repeated growth and a final full copy. The public byte[] contract and wire compatibility make the final owned array necessary; any optimization must preserve format version, field ordering, encoding, and exception behavior.

finding.summary: Compression negotiation fully sorts candidates to select one provider.
finding.explanation: On the multi-candidate request path, the code orders every ProviderCandidate by quality and priority and immediately takes First(). A single-pass best-candidate selection would avoid the full sort. The expected candidate set is normally small, so the occurrence is retained at low severity despite being on a per-request path.

finding.summary: WebTransport session disposal blocks on each stream’s asynchronous disposal while holding the stream lock.
finding.explanation: The synchronous session Dispose path calls DisposeAsync().AsTask().GetAwaiter().GetResult() for every open stream while holding _openStreams. WebTransportStream disposal awaits registration and pipe completion, so this can block a shared server thread and prolong lock ownership for every stream in the session.

finding.summary: WebTransport stream removal synchronously blocks on asynchronous disposal.
finding.explanation: TryRemoveStream is a reusable per-stream server path and converts WebTransportStream.DisposeAsync into a blocking wait. The disposal performs genuinely asynchronous registration and pipe completion work, so a connection-processing thread can be occupied while continuations complete.

finding.summary: The JSON converter activates TMessage through a generic new() constraint for every deserialization.
finding.explanation: ListValueConverter<TMessage>.Read is a per-message deserialization path and constructs each message with new TMessage(). This is the card's exact generic activation shape on a high-volume parser path.

finding.summary: Iterator-symbol membership repeatedly scans a retained list.
finding.explanation: IsIterator performs List<ILocalSymbol>.Any with symbol equality. It is called while analyzer state is populated and from the ReportDiagnostics Where predicate for every recorded occurrence, producing repeated linear scans as nested-loop state grows.

finding.summary: Potential-iterator duplicate checks repeatedly scan a growing list.
finding.explanation: IsPotentialIterator searches PotentialIterators with Any and is invoked for each candidate added by the analyzer. The retained sequential list can grow with the number of variables in nested loops, making duplicate checks quadratic in the candidate count.
finding.snippet: return target is not null && PotentialIterators.Any(existing => SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(existing, target));

finding.summary: Each related variable reference rescans all retained for-loop variables.
finding.explanation: AddRelatedOccurrences loops over variableReferences and calls Any on the retained AllForVariables list for every reference. This is the card's explicit nested sequential-search shape and scales as references multiplied by tracked variables.

finding.summary: Root-component operation duplicate detection scans all prior IDs.
finding.explanation: TryDeserializeRootComponentOperations loops over every operation and calls Span<int>.Contains on the prefix containing all previously seen component IDs. Unique batches therefore perform 0+1+...+(N-1) comparisons. The code even supports batches larger than 128 via ArrayPool, so the quadratic shape is not limited to tiny stack-only inputs.

finding.summary: Request culture resolution linearly scans the supported-culture list for every requested culture candidate.
finding.explanation: On the middleware request path, GetCultureInfo iterates provider-supplied cultureNames and calls this helper for each candidate. The helper uses FirstOrDefault over the retained IList<CultureInfo>, so N requested names and M supported cultures produce O(N x M) comparisons; parent-culture fallback can repeat the scan. A precomputed lookup must preserve ordinal-ignore-case matching, configured order/duplicates, and read-only CultureInfo wrapping.
finding.snippet:
var culture = supportedCultures.FirstOrDefault(
    supportedCulture => StringSegment.Equals(supportedCulture.Name, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

finding.summary: Validation-summary fallback rescans a growing list for every model-state entry.
finding.explanation: GetModelStateList builds a List<ModelStateEntry> using Visit. When entries.Count is less than ModelState.Count, it iterates the entire model-state dictionary and performs entries.Contains(entry.Value) on each iteration. Each membership operation scans the retained list, which grows as unmatched entries are appended. This has quadratic worst-case comparison cost in that fallback branch. DefaultHtmlGenerator.GenerateValidationSummary calls the helper at line 844. Build a HashSet<ModelStateEntry> only when the fallback is required and retain the list for rendering order, using the same default equality semantics. Branch reachability and timing have not been exercised at runtime.
finding.recommended_fix: Only when entering the unmatched-entry fallback, build a HashSet<ModelStateEntry> alongside the ordered rendering list.
finding.compatibility_notes: Preserve default equality semantics, rendering order, and the existing list contract. The model-binding producer and runtime impact remain unverified.

notes: Investigating real model-binding production of unmatched entries and actual validation-summary output before optimizing the linear membership fallback. Directly injecting ModelState callbacks/entries alone does not establish producer reachability.

finding.summary: Allowed claim values are linearly rescanned for each user claim.
finding.explanation: HasMatchingClaim iterates the user claims and calls IsMatch for each claim. finding.summary: Group-exclusion sends rescan the excluded connection list for every group connection.
finding.explanation: SendGroupExceptAsync passes an IReadOnlyList<string>.Contains predicate to SendToGroupConnections. That helper invokes the predicate inside its foreach over group connections, producing O(group connections x excluded IDs) comparisons for sequential list/array inputs.

finding.summary: Broadcast exclusions rescan the excluded connection list for every connection.
finding.explanation: SendAllExceptAsync passes a sequential Contains predicate to SendToAllConnections, which executes it inside the foreach over the connection store. With ordinary IReadOnlyList implementations this repeats a linear exclusion scan once per connected client.
finding.snippet: return SendToAllConnections(methodName, args, (connection, state) => !((IReadOnlyList<string>)state!).Contains(connection.ConnectionId), excludedConnectionIds, cancellationToken);

finding.summary: Large targeted sends rescan the requested connection list for every connected client.
finding.explanation: For more than 16 requested IDs, SendConnectionsAsync intentionally routes through SendToAllConnections and calls IReadOnlyList<string>.Contains for each connection. This is the card's repeated sequential membership shape and can scale O(all connections x requested IDs). The source documents an allocation tradeoff, so any fix must retain a small/large-list strategy and preserve deduplication and send-once semantics.
finding.snippet: return SendToAllConnections(methodName, args, (connection, state) => ((IReadOnlyList<string>)state!).Contains(connection.ConnectionId), connectionIds, cancellationToken);

finding.summary: SignalR repeatedly scans recipient and exclusion lists while iterating connections.
finding.explanation: SendUsersAsync passes an IReadOnlyList<string>.Contains predicate to SendToAllConnections, which invokes it for each connection. With ordinary array/list inputs, this performs up to N*M membership comparisons for N connections and M user IDs. SendAllExceptAsync at line 318 and SendGroupExceptAsync at line 264 use the same repeated linear-exclusion shape. Build a membership index once per send when list size and connection count amortize its allocation; retain a small-list fast path and preserve ordinal comparison, duplicates, null user identifiers, and send-once semantics. The large-list SendConnectionsAsync branch explicitly trades lookup work for bounded allocation and is not presented as an unconditional defect. Confirmed denotes source shape, not a measured throughput regression.
finding.snippet: return SendToAllConnections(methodName, args, (connection, state) => ((IReadOnlyList<string>)state!).Contains(connection.UserIdentifier), userIds, cancellationToken);
finding.recommended_fix: Build an ordinal membership set once per send when list size and connection count amortize its allocation; retain a small-list fast path.
finding.compatibility_notes: Preserve duplicates, null user identifiers, send-once behavior, and explicit allocation tradeoffs. HashSet is portable. This is source-level complexity evidence, not measured throughput.

finding.summary: Legacy managed encryption grows a default MemoryStream and then copies it with ToArray.
finding.explanation: On the non-NET target branches, each Encrypt call accumulates a caller-sized protected payload in a default-capacity MemoryStream through direct and CryptoStream writes, then makes a second full copy with ToArray. The final output size is derivable from the plaintext length, block size, header, and MAC, so large inputs can trigger avoidable growth copies and peak memory. The net12.0 branch already uses a sized pooled writer and is not affected.

finding.summary: Legacy managed decryption grows a default MemoryStream and then copies it with ToArray.
finding.explanation: On the non-NET target branches, each Decrypt call writes the caller-sized plaintext through a CryptoStream into a default-capacity MemoryStream and then copies the complete buffer with ToArray. The plaintext length is available from the protected-payload layout, so large inputs can cause avoidable resizing, copying, and peak memory. The net12.0 branch already uses a sized pooled writer and is not affected.

finding.summary: Google user-information JSON is materialized as a string before stream-capable parsing.
finding.explanation: The authentication handler reads the complete HTTP response body into a string and immediately passes that throwaway string to JsonDocument.Parse. This runs while creating an authentication ticket, and the net12.0 project can parse the response content stream directly while preserving response cancellation and document lifetime.

finding.summary: Nested layout metadata is rediscovered through reflection on every render.
finding.explanation: Render walks the layout chain whenever parameters are set, and every level calls GetCustomAttribute<LayoutAttribute>() without a per-Type cache. Layout parentage is immutable metadata, so repeated component renders redo reflection lookup and attribute materialization for the same layout types.

finding.summary: JSON Patch list operations rediscover IList<T> metadata for each operation.
finding.explanation: TryGetListTypeArgument obtains list.GetType() and calls ClosedGenericMatcher.ExtractGenericInterface for IList<> every time a list operation needs its element type. JSON Patch can perform multiple operations against the same runtime list type, so interface discovery and generic metadata traversal repeat on the operation path. Cache the resolved element type or unsupported result by runtime Type while preserving arrays/non-generic-list errors, trimming behavior, and serializer conversion semantics.

finding.summary: Enum values use repeated closed-generic reflection and MethodInfo.Invoke.
finding.explanation: GetCurrentValues runs while rendering select inputs and, for each nonempty string enum value, closes the same generic method for the model enum type and invokes it reflectively. The open MethodInfo is cached, but the closed method/delegate and dispatch are not cached per enum type.
finding.snippet:
var methodInfo = ConvertEnumFromStringMethod.MakeGenericMethod(innerType);
enumValue = (Enum)methodInfo.Invoke(obj: null, parameters: new[] { stringValue });

notes: Investigating a non-reflective Enum.TryParse(Type,...) replacement for per-value MakeGenericMethod/Invoke. No new type cache planned. Establish actual binding/selection behavior for enum names, numeric values, aliases, flags, invalid values and nullable/multiple selection before implementation.

finding.summary: Synchronous response writes block on asynchronous response-start work.
finding.explanation: ResponseStream.Write performs the same synchronous wait on the asynchronous _onStart callback before each first synchronous write. This is a reusable request/response path, so a pending start operation blocks a throughput-bearing thread.

The owning collection is internal, so the proposed concrete path does not alter the exported framework API. Interface consumers still box; the benefit applies to the inspected concrete evaluator loop. No runtime benchmark was run.

finding.summary: JSON Patch value conversion allocates a JSON string solely to deserialize it into the property type.
finding.explanation: ConvertTo short-circuits null and assignable values, but both non-assignable branches call SerializeObject(value) directly inside DeserializeObject. JsonPatchDocument.ApplyTo loops through operations; Operation.Apply dispatches Add, ObjectAdapter.Add resolves the target adapter, and PocoAdapter.TryAdd calls TryConvertValue, which calls this helper. Thus conversion can allocate and process a throwaway JSON string for each applicable patch operation. The serializer conversion itself is intentional; this finding concerns its text bridge, not a proposal to remove conversion or preserve mutable aliases. No throughput or allocation trace was run, and gains from a token-based bridge remain unmeasured.
finding.recommended_fix: Within the existing internal conversion seam, evaluate a Json.NET JTokenWriter/JTokenReader bridge (or direct ToObject for compatible already-materialized tokens) instead of allocating JSON text. Retain the assignability fast path and public signatures. Use separate serialization and deserialization configurations matching the current defaults and supplied resolver, and preserve the fallback where direct conversion changes semantics. Do not replace CopyTo with returning the original mutable value.
finding.compatibility_notes: Json.NET token readers/writers are package APIs available across this project's net462, netstandard2.0 and net12.0 targets; no modern-only BCL API or public API redesign is required. Consequently, foreach over a concrete ValidationStateDictionary cannot use Dictionary's allocation-free pattern enumerator; impact depends on concrete-type iteration frequency in validation paths.

finding.summary: Enum-name metadata is reverse-scanned for every selected enum value.
finding.explanation: Inside the raw-values loop, the code scans the entire EnumNamesAndValues dictionary by value to recover every matching name. Rendering multi-select enum values therefore repeats an O(enum-members) scan per selected value; enum sizes are usually small, so impact is classified likely rather than confirmed high severity.

finding.summary: GetFiles allocates a new List even when no form files match the requested name.
finding.explanation: The per-request collection query eagerly creates List<IFormFile> before it knows whether any item matches. The returned contract is IReadOnlyList<IFormFile>, so the common empty-result case can use shared immutable empty storage while allocating a list only after the first match; actual no-match frequency is workload-dependent.

finding.summary: Cookie header values are copied to an array for a single join operation.
finding.explanation: MergeCookies runs while processing request headers and materializes StringValues with ToArray only to pass the result once to string.Join. The IEnumerable join overload can consume the values without the temporary array, although the specialized array overload may have different constant-factor costs; that tradeoff makes this a likely rather than confirmed finding.

finding.summary: Invalid Identity tokens are rejected through a broad exception-driven validation path.
finding.explanation: ValidateAsync treats invalid external token data as a normal false result, but Base64 decoding, data unprotection, and binary reads execute inside a catch-all block. Malformed tokens therefore incur exception and stack-unwind costs; non-throwing validation can at least reject malformed Base64 before entering the unavoidable protection/parser exception boundary. The impact depends on invalid-token frequency.

finding.summary: Option rendering can linearly rescan caller-supplied selected values.
finding.explanation: GenerateOption is called once per SelectListItem and invokes ICollection<string>.Contains for each option. The normal internal GetCurrentValues path supplies a HashSet, but the public GenerateSelect overload accepts any ICollection<string>; a List or other sequential collection turns option generation into O(options × selected-values) work.

finding.summary: Stored component/TempData serialization grows a contiguous MemoryStream and then copies the full payload.
finding.explanation: SerializeData and SerializeValue construct default growable MemoryStreams, write JSON through Utf8JsonWriter and return ToArray. Allowed values include strings and collections, with no size bound in this serializer. SessionStorageTempDataProvider.SaveTempData serializes nonempty data before session.Set, establishing a persistence request consumer. Large encoded data can therefore cause backing-array growth copies plus an exact result copy; actual payload frequency and allocation magnitude remain unmeasured.
finding.recommended_fix: Consider an internal pooled/segmented UTF-8 buffer writer and make only the final independent byte[] copy required by IStoredDataSerializer. If a valid exact encoded length is available, pre-size instead. Do not remove the owned byte[] boundary or impose new limits without the storage contract permitting it.
finding.compatibility_notes: Keep JSON type tokens, options, ordering, complete output before storage, exception timing and independent array ownership. Utf8JsonWriter accepts IBufferWriter<byte> on the existing modern target; pooled scratch storage needs deterministic return and bounded retention. No public API change is recommended.

finding.summary: Stored single-value serialization uses a growable MemoryStream followed by ToArray.
finding.explanation: SerializeValue independently creates a default MemoryStream, writes an allowed value through Utf8JsonWriter, and returns a full ToArray copy. The value contract permits strings and collections without a local encoded-size bound, so large values can cause growth copies and LOH pressure. The fix boundary must preserve the exact owned byte[] result and all existing JSON token and converter behavior.

finding.summary: Distributed cache tag-helper encoding grows a MemoryStream despite knowing the final byte count.
finding.explanation: Encode appends a four-byte key length, serializedKey, and value to a default MemoryStream and returns ToArray. The exact result size is known before writing, while cached content can be large, so the current shape can resize and then copy the entire payload. Pre-sizing or writing directly into one exact byte[] can preserve the binary format and independent ownership without growth copies.

finding.summary: OpenAPI body-parameter selection fully counts a filtered sequence to test uniqueness.

finding.recommended_fix: Use one enumeration that remembers the first matching body parameter and stops upon finding a second.
finding.compatibility_notes: Return false and retain a null out parameter for zero or multiple matches. Any alone and SingleOrDefault are not equivalent. Parameter lists are typically short.
